per_depth.common_affordance: The promise that every input has exactly one of two explicitly stated, independently checkable certificate types
The guarantee that exactly one violation exists, allowing JOB violations to be handled by early return and LOAD 2 to be inferred after LOAD 1 is absent.
The statement directly exposes that every accepted certificate is obtained by one of two scalar threshold tests: a single item's p1 + p2 versus T or a stage-wide sum versus T.
The statement directly exposes an exhaustive classification by two trivial lower bounds: an individual job's p1+p2 and each stage's total workload.
The statement exposes that each relaxed feasibility question is decided by direct additive duration bounds: p1+p2>T for JOB i and the total duration on a stage exceeding T for LOAD c.
The statement explicitly decomposes the answer into an independently tested per-item JOB condition or per-component LOAD condition.
The signals are rectangular intervals on a single continuous bounded line, so non-overlap is characterized solely by sums of widths.
The intrinsic reduction of interval isometries to image intervals of identical lengths, turning JOB into p1+p2>T and LOAD into the total component-length test.

The intrinsic pigeonhole characterization of exact-cardinality subsets of the finite window [1,T], with strict precedence forcing p_i,1+p_i,2 distinct slots for a job and core exclusivity forcing the per-core cardinalities to sum to at most T.
The statement decomposes feasibility into independent cardinality tests: one graph is feasible iff p_i1+p_i2<=T, and a phase is feasible across graphs iff its demands sum to at most T.
